name: Diyaluma Falls
accessibility: Roadside view from the Colombo-Batticaloa highway; hiking to the top pools requires a strenuous 1-2 hour climb
description: Diyaluma is the second-highest waterfall in Sri Lanka, cascading dramatically down a rock face beside the main highway between Wellawaya and Koslanda. Adventurous visitors can hike up to a series of natural infinity pools at the top, offering panoramic views over the Uva lowlands. The base area has a small pool for a quick dip, while the top pools are a favorite for cliff-jumping and swimming among backpackers.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Bambarakanda Falls
accessibility: Short walk from the parking area near Kalupahana; base viewpoint is easily accessible
description: Bambarakanda is the tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka, plunging 241 meters down a forested cliff near Kalupahana in the hill country. The falls are fed by the Kuda Oya stream and are most powerful during the northeast monsoon season. A short trail from the road leads to a viewing point at the base, and the surrounding pine forest makes it a popular stop for hikers heading to nearby tea estates.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Dunhinda Falls
accessibility: 15-20 minute walk on a paved path from the entrance near Badulla
description: Dunhinda Falls is one of the most scenic waterfalls in Sri Lanka, located a short drive from Badulla town. Water from the Badulu Oya river drops in a broad curtain into a misty pool below, creating a fine spray that gives the falls its bridal-veil appearance. The walk to the falls passes through forest and small stalls selling snacks, making it an easy and popular family outing.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Ravana Falls
accessibility: Directly visible from the Ella-Wellawaya highway, roadside viewing platform
description: Ravana Falls is a wide, low waterfall located right beside the main road near Ella, making it one of the most accessible falls in the hill country. Local legend connects the falls to the Ramayana epic, adding cultural significance to its natural beauty. Visitors often stop briefly for photos, though swimming is discouraged due to strong currents, especially after rain.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: St. Clair's Falls
accessibility: Roadside viewpoint on the Talawakele-Ginigathena road
description: Known as the 'Little Niagara of Sri Lanka', St. Clair's Falls is a broad twin waterfall set amid rolling tea plantations near Talawakele. Its wide curtain of water and lush green surroundings make it one of the most photographed falls in the country, easily viewed from a roadside platform without any hiking required. The falls are especially striking after the monsoon rains fill the Kotmale Oya.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Devon Falls
accessibility: Roadside viewpoint on the Hatton-Talawakele road
description: Devon Falls drops 97 meters through a narrow gorge surrounded by tea estates, located close to St. Clair's Falls in the hill country. Named after an early British coffee planter, the falls are visible from a roadside lookout point and are a common stop on hill-country road trips. The dramatic single drop is best viewed from a distance across the valley.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Bopath Ella Falls
accessibility: Short walk from the parking area near Kuruwita
description: Bopath Ella takes its name from its distinctive leaf-shaped silhouette, resembling a Bo leaf as it falls into a wide pool below. Located near Kuruwita in Ratnapura district, the falls are a popular local swimming and picnic spot, easily reached by a short walk from the road. The pool at the base is generally calm enough for casual bathing outside of peak monsoon flow.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Laxapana Falls
accessibility: Roadside viewpoint near Maskeliya
description: Laxapana Falls is formed by the Maskeliya Oya and is closely tied to Sri Lanka's hydroelectric power history, feeding one of the country's earliest hydro plants. The falls can be viewed from a roadside point along the Hatton-Maskeliya road, set against a backdrop of forested hills. Its consistent flow makes it visible throughout the year, unlike some seasonal falls nearby.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Aberdeen Falls
accessibility: Short hike required from the nearest access road
description: Aberdeen Falls is a scenic multi-tier waterfall near the Aberdeen hydro reservoir in the Kegalle district, reached via a short but sometimes steep forest path. The falls feed into the Aberdeen reservoir, part of the Kotmale hydroelectric complex, and are less crowded than more famous falls, offering a quieter nature experience. The surrounding forest and stream crossings add to the hike's appeal.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Galboda Falls
accessibility: Hike through forest trail required
description: Galboda Falls lies close to Aberdeen Falls in the Kegalle hills and requires a forest walk to reach, keeping visitor numbers relatively low. The falls tumble over a rocky outcrop into a shaded pool, popular with local hikers exploring the Kotmale watershed area. Both Galboda and Aberdeen are often visited together as part of a half-day hiking trip.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
accessibility: Overnight pilgrimage climb via ~5500 steps, well-lit during pilgrim season Dec-May
description: Adam's Peak, known locally as Sri Pada, is one of Sri Lanka's most sacred mountains, revered by Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, and Christians alike for the sacred footprint at its summit. Pilgrims typically begin the climb at night to reach the summit by sunrise, witnessing the famous shadow of the peak cast across the clouds. The pilgrimage season runs from December to May, when the thousands of steps are illuminated and lined with tea stalls.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Pidurutalagala
accessibility: Highest peak in Sri Lanka; summit road is military-restricted, special permission required
description: Pidurutalagala is the highest mountain in Sri Lanka, towering above Nuwara Eliya town. Its summit hosts telecommunications towers and is controlled by the military, meaning public access is restricted and usually requires prior permission or a guided tour. The lower slopes offer forest trails and cool climate scenery typical of the central highlands.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Ella Rock
accessibility: Popular day hike from Ella town, ~3-4 hours round trip via the railway track route
description: Ella Rock is one of the most popular day hikes in the hill country, offering sweeping views over the Ella Gap and surrounding tea country. The trail often begins by following the railway tracks out of Ella before climbing through forest and tea estates to the summit. It's a moderately challenging but non-technical hike, making it accessible to most reasonably fit travelers.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Namunukula
accessibility: Full-day hike across a seven-peak ridge, guide recommended
description: Namunukula is a distinctive seven-peaked mountain range near Badulla, forming one of the highest points in Uva province. The ridge hike traverses multiple summits and offers panoramic views across the eastern hill country toward the lowlands. Due to its length and lack of clear signage in places, a local guide is recommended for the full traverse.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Hanthana Mountain Range
accessibility: Multiple trailheads accessible from Kandy city, various loop options
description: The Hanthana range lies just outside Kandy city, offering a network of hiking trails through forest reserves and old tea and cardamom plantations. Popular routes include the Panorama Route and trails past the University of Peradeniya, with several viewpoints overlooking Kandy and the surrounding hills. Its proximity to the city makes it a favorite for both casual walkers and serious trail runners.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: World's End (Horton Plains)
accessibility: Park entrance fee applies (~USD 35 for foreign adults); circular trail from the entrance, ~3-4 hours
description: World's End is a sheer escarpment within Horton Plains National Park, dropping nearly 880 meters into the valley below and offering one of the most dramatic views in Sri Lanka. The trail to World's End follows a circular route through montane grasslands and cloud forest, passing Baker's Falls along the way. Early morning visits are recommended, as mist typically rolls in and obscures the view by mid-morning.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Riverston Peak
accessibility: Viewpoint accessible by road with short walks to lookout points
description: Riverston, part of the Knuckles mountain range, is known for its dramatic rock formations and panoramic viewpoints, most famously 'Mini World's End'. The area offers a mix of short roadside viewpoints and longer hiking trails through cloud forest, making it flexible for different fitness levels. Riverston is also a gateway for more serious treks into the Knuckles range.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Lakegala
accessibility: Technical climb with exposed rock sections; local guide strongly recommended
description: Lakegala is a striking, near-vertical rock peak within the Knuckles range, considered one of the more technical and challenging climbs in Sri Lanka. The final ascent involves scrambling over exposed rock faces, and the mountain holds cultural significance in local Ravana-related folklore. Due to the terrain, only experienced hikers with a knowledgeable local guide should attempt the summit.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Kirigalpotta
accessibility: Second-highest peak in Sri Lanka; permit from Horton Plains park office required
description: Kirigalpotta is the second-highest mountain in Sri Lanka, located within the Horton Plains National Park boundary. Unlike World's End, reaching the summit requires special permission from park authorities and a longer trek through denser forest and grassland. Its relative inaccessibility keeps visitor numbers low compared to other Horton Plains attractions.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Knuckles Peak
accessibility: Multi-hour trek from designated trailheads within the Knuckles Conservation Forest
description: Knuckles Peak is the central and highest point of the Knuckles mountain range, named for its resemblance to a clenched fist when viewed from a distance. The range is a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its exceptional biodiversity and cloud forest ecosystems. Treks to the peak pass through varied terrain, from grasslands to dense montane forest, and are best done with a registered guide.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Mirissa Beach
accessibility: Easily accessible from Mirissa town, close to Matara-Colombo coastal road
description: Mirissa is a crescent-shaped beach on the south coast famous for its calm waters, palm-lined shore, and vibrant beach bar scene. It's one of the best departure points in Sri Lanka for whale and dolphin watching boat tours, especially for spotting blue whales during the season. The beach is also popular with surfers at its western end, near Parrot Rock.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Unawatuna Beach
accessibility: A few kilometers from Galle Fort, easily reached by tuk-tuk or bus
description: Unawatuna is a sheltered horseshoe-shaped bay near Galle, known for its calm, shallow waters that make it one of the safest swimming beaches in Sri Lanka. The beach is lined with guesthouses, cafes, and dive shops, and is a popular base for snorkeling trips to nearby coral reefs. Its proximity to Galle Fort makes it a convenient stop on south coast itineraries.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Hikkaduwa Beach
accessibility: Directly accessible from Hikkaduwa town along the coastal road
description: Hikkaduwa is known for its coral sanctuary and lively surf scene, combining a protected marine national park with a bustling stretch of beach bars and shops. Glass-bottom boat tours and snorkeling trips let visitors view the coral reef and its resident sea turtles just offshore. The southern end of the beach also offers consistent waves popular with both beginner and experienced surfers.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Bentota Beach
accessibility: Well connected via the Southern Expressway and coastal railway
description: Bentota is one of Sri Lanka's premier beach resort towns, known for its wide sandy shore and extensive water sports offerings, including jet skiing, windsurfing, and deep-sea fishing. The Bentota river estuary nearby adds river safari and mangrove tour options alongside the beach itself. Large resort hotels line much of the coastline, making it a popular choice for package holidaymakers.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Arugam Bay
accessibility: Located on the east coast; best reached via Pottuvil, road access from Colombo ~7-8 hours
description: Arugam Bay is widely regarded as one of the best surf destinations in South Asia, drawing surfers from around the world to its consistent right-hand point break. Beyond surfing, the area offers a laid-back beach town atmosphere, nearby lagoons for birdwatching, and easy access to Kumana National Park. The surf season runs opposite to the west and south coasts, peaking during the southwest monsoon.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Nilaveli Beach
accessibility: A short drive north of Trincomalee town
description: Nilaveli is a long stretch of white sand beach on the northeast coast, known for its calm, clear waters and proximity to Pigeon Island National Park. Boat trips from Nilaveli take visitors to Pigeon Island for snorkeling among coral reefs and reef sharks. The relatively undeveloped coastline gives it a quieter feel compared to more built-up west coast beaches.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Pasikuda Beach
accessibility: Accessible via Batticaloa or Valachchenai on the east coast
description: Pasikuda is known for its unusually shallow, calm bay, where the sea remains gentle far from shore, making it especially popular with families and less confident swimmers. The beach has seen significant resort development in recent years while retaining long stretches of quiet sand further from the main hotel strip. Its calm waters also make it suitable for kayaking and paddleboarding.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Tangalle Beach
accessibility: Along the southern coastal road east of Matara
description: Tangalle offers some of the south coast's quieter, less developed beaches, with several secluded coves separated by rocky outcrops. Nearby beaches such as Rekawa are important sea turtle nesting sites, with guided night tours available to watch turtles come ashore to lay eggs. The area's relative remoteness compared to Mirissa or Unawatuna appeals to travelers seeking a slower pace.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Weligama Beach
accessibility: On the main coastal road between Galle and Matara
description: Weligama's wide, gently sloping bay makes it one of the best places in Sri Lanka to learn surfing, with numerous surf schools catering to beginners. The bay also has iconic offshore stilt fishermen, a traditional fishing method now largely maintained for tourism photography. Its calmer, more forgiving waves contrast with the more advanced breaks found elsewhere on the south coast.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Negombo Beach
accessibility: Close to Bandaranaike International Airport, ~20-30 minutes drive
description: Negombo is a popular first or last stop for travelers due to its proximity to Colombo's international airport, offering a long sandy beach and a historic fishing town atmosphere. The town's fish market and Dutch canal system reflect its colonial-era trading history, alongside a busy modern tourist strip of hotels and restaurants. It's a convenient base for travelers with limited time before a flight.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Trincomalee Beach
accessibility: Accessible within Trincomalee town, including Uppuveli and Dutch Bay areas
description: Trincomalee sits on one of the world's finest natural deep-water harbours, with nearby beaches like Uppuveli and Dutch Bay offering calm swimming and diving conditions. The area is rich in history, home to the historic Koneswaram temple and remnants of Dutch and British colonial forts. Diving and snorkeling trips explore nearby wrecks and reefs, taking advantage of the sheltered harbour waters.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Hiriketiya Beach
accessibility: Short detour from the main road near Dickwella
description: Hiriketiya is a small horseshoe-shaped bay that has become a favorite among surfers and digital nomads for its consistent, beginner-friendly waves and relaxed cafe scene. The compact bay is surrounded by cliffs and coconut palms, giving it a more intimate feel than larger south coast beaches. Its rise in popularity has brought a wave of boutique guesthouses and yoga retreats to the area.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Talalla Beach
accessibility: Located between Matara and Dickwella on the southern coastal road
description: Talalla is a long, uncrowded stretch of beach known for its calm, clean waters and quieter atmosphere compared to more touristy south coast spots. It has become known for yoga retreats and wellness-focused guesthouses that take advantage of the peaceful setting. The relatively flat, gentle surf makes it suitable for casual swimming rather than serious surfing.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image

name: Kalpitiya Beach
accessibility: Accessible via Puttalam, ~3 hours drive from Colombo
description: Kalpitiya is Sri Lanka's premier kitesurfing destination, benefiting from strong, consistent winds during the southwest monsoon season across its lagoon and open coastline. The area is also known for dolphin watching tours in the Kalpitiya lagoon, alongside a growing number of eco-lodges and kite schools. Its relatively undeveloped, laid-back character sets it apart from the more built-up west coast resort towns.
image_source_attribution: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA - verify per image
